name: Fedora
warning: A quick post install guide has to be followed to make the most out of the system; Does not come with proprietary codecs and drivers by default.
description: A professional, up-to-date system that balances the newest features with reliability. It is often used as a testing ground for future corporate technologies but remains stable enough for daily use.

name: Nobara
description: A modified version of Fedora designed specifically for gamers and content creators. It comes pre-fixed and set up so you can start playing games immediately without technical hassles.

name: Linux Mint
warning: Expect screen tearing and poor fractional scaling on high-res or mixed-refresh-rate monitors.
description: Built for stability and ease of use. It looks and feels very similar to Windows, making it the perfect choice for people trying Linux for the first time.

name: LMDE
warning: Expect screen tearing and poor fractional scaling on high-res or mixed-refresh-rate monitors.
description: A version of Linux Mint that works exactly the same way but is built on a different, slightly more independent foundation for those who prefer an alternative technical base.

name: Ubuntu
warning: Current LTS release removed the driver manager without a good replacement.
description: The most popular version of Linux. It is very easy to find help online, has strong professional support, and uses its own easy-to-use software store system.

name: Pop!_OS
description: Designed for science, engineering, and creative work. It manages windows automatically to help you focus and handles graphics card drivers for you right out of the box.

name: Arch Linux
warning: Arch Linux servers experience a lot of downtime; The AUR recently had a malware attack.
description: A build-it-yourself system that gives you total control. You install it mostly manually and choose exactly what parts you want. Recommended for advanced users who want to learn how Linux works.

name: Omarchy
description: A version of Arch Linux that comes pre-configured with a fancy look. It saves you the trouble of setting up complex window arrangements manually.

name: CachyOS
description: Built specifically for speed. It uses special technical optimizations to make games and heavy programs run faster than on standard systems.

name: Debian
description: Known as the 'universal' system because it is incredibly stable and reliable. Ideally suited for servers or computers that need to run for a long time without issues, though it might not have the newest features immediately.

name: Bazzite
description: Designed to turn your computer or handheld into a gaming console. It mimics the experience of the Steam Deck, focusing entirely on gaming ease of use.

name: Fedora Atomic
description: A version of Fedora designed to be unbreakable. The core system is locked down so you can't accidentally damage it, making it very safe and reliable.

name: Gentoo
description: A system for experts that builds every program specifically for your computer's hardware. It takes a long time to install things, but it offers the ultimate level of customization.

name: NixOS
description: A unique system where you manage settings using a single text file. If something breaks, you can instantly go back to a previous working state. It is very different from other Linux versions.

name: Void
description: An independent system built from scratch. It is known for being very fast, lightweight, and responsive, aimed at users who want a simple but powerful computer.

name: Slackware
description: The oldest Linux version still in use. It does not do things automatically for you, requiring you to manage software manually. It is great for learning how the old-school basics work.

name: Zorin OS
warning: It is currently not possible to switch from their paid version to the free tier, requiring Pro Users to purchase a new license with every major release to stay up to date.
description: Designed specifically to help people switching from Windows or macOS. It is very polished and lets you choose a look that feels familiar to what you used before.

name: OpenSUSE Leap
description: A professional-grade system that shares its foundation with corporate servers. It is extremely stable and great for getting work done without surprises.

name: OpenSUSE Tumbleweed
description: Gives you the very latest software updates as soon as they are available. It uses automatic testing to make sure these new updates don't break your computer.

name: OpenSUSE microOS
description: Aeon Desktop is an immutable, GNOME-centric Linux distribution that protects its core system with transactional updates while relying on Flatpaks and Distrobox for containerized applications and development workflows.

name: EndeavourOS
description: Makes the powerful Arch Linux system easy to install. It gives you a clean start but still requires you to use the text command line occasionally.

name: Manjaro
warning: Holding back updates by 2 weeks often causes library version mismatches (glibc) with the AUR. Software installed via AUR frequently breaks after system updates.
description: A user-friendly version of Arch Linux. It tests updates longer to ensure stability and includes easy graphical tools to manage hardware drivers without using text commands.

name: Garuda
description: Garuda Linux is a performance-oriented, Arch-based distribution designed for gamers and enthusiasts that combines a visually striking neon aesthetic with user-friendly GUI tools and automatic system snapshots.

name: Rocky Linux
description: Rocky Linux is a community-driven, enterprise-grade operating system designed to serve as a rock-solid, binary-compatible downstream alternative to Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL).

name: Red Hat Enterprise Linux
description: A paid, highly reliable operating system designed for businesses that require guaranteed technical support.

name: Oracle Linux
description: A paid, highly reliable operating system designed for businesses that require guaranteed technical support.
